currentContext.strategies: Optimise power cost, which is the dominant cost lever for a power-intensive chlor-alkali business, by raising the share of renewable energy in the mix through group-captive and SPV structures with GIPCL, Aditya Birla Renewables and Clean Max Sphere Energy, plus short/medium-term solar purchases from NVVNL, Tata Power, Kreate Energy and P R Energy|Upgrade old-generation electrolysers to the latest-generation membrane cell technology (4th generation to 6th generation B+ elements, and a placed order to replace 590 old 4B cell elements with energy-efficient 6B+ elements) to lower specific power consumption and manufacturing cost|Strengthen downstream integration and captive chlorine consumption through the chlorotoluenes chain, with the Chlorotoluene Downstream Project under implementation|Convert caustic soda from liquid to solid form via a latest-technology Flaker Unit with a view to enhancing export potential|Grow exports as a structural channel, having achieved ever-highest exports of Rs.946 Crores standalone and Rs.1242 Crores including GNAL|Drive R&D-led import substitution and alternate sourcing for critical raw materials such as rock phosphate and amyl alcohol, alongside development of value-added products (dibenzyl ether, MKP, DKP, TKP, benzyl acetate, sodium benzoate, benzyl salicylate) that have reached pilot scale|Pursue collaborative research with BITS Pilani Goa Campus, CSMCRI and NACL Industries Limited focused on waste utilization, sustainable technologies and value-added products|Expand renewable capacity further, including an MOU signed with GMDC to explore additional renewable assets in SPV mode, and continuing discussions with RE developers to tie up further RE projects
currentContext.expansion: GACL is pursuing a structured growth strategy focused on portfolio diversification, value addition to its chlorine chain, higher captive chlorine consumption and operational flexibility. The 30 KTPA Chlorotoluenes Plant at Dahej, described as India's largest integrated facility for Benzyl Chloride, Benzyl Alcohol and Benzaldehyde, ramped up significantly during FY 2025-26 to approximately 80% capacity utilisation and is expected to run at full capacity in FY 2026-27; the Hydrazine Hydrate Plant remains under stabilisation. A 40 TPD Chlorotoluenes Downstream Project is being implemented at Dahej for 2 downstream products in phase-I, the third product originally envisaged having been dropped. A 200 TPD Caustic Soda Flaking Unit and a 120 TPD Hydrochloric Acid Synthesis Unit are being installed and are expected to be commissioned by the end of FY 2026-27, alongside investments in a new boiler facility and replacement of selected electrolyser cell elements with next-generation energy-efficient cell technology (an order was placed for 590 old 4B elements to be replaced with 6B+ elements, imported via Thyssenkrupp Nucera India). Building on the existing Food Grade Phosphoric Acid facility, an additional 33,870 TPA Food Grade Phosphoric Acid plant is planned at Dahej. Caustic Potash capacity at Vadodara is being enhanced by converting existing caustic soda cells, with electrolyser reallocation raising Potassium Hydroxide capacity from 120 TPD to 200 TPD. A 5,000 TPA High Purity / Electronic Grade Hydrogen Peroxide facility is being set up to serve semiconductor, electronics and high-purity chemical demand. During FY 2026-27 the Company plans to commission the HCl Synthesis Unit, Chlorotoluene Downstream Plant, Caustic Soda Flaking Plant and Cell Element Replacement Project. On power, a 75 MW Group Captive Solar Power Plant with GIPCL and GSFC was commissioned in two phases (25 MW in April 2025 and 50 MW in June 2025), with GACL holding a 37.5 MW (50%) share; a 62.7 MW hybrid SPV with Aditya Birla Renewable Energy is expected operational by around October 2026 / Q2 FY 2026-27; and a 75.9 MW hybrid SPV with Clean Max is phased with 16.5 MW by October 2026 and 59.4 MW by March 2027. The Company is further evaluating proposals for up to 100 MW (minimum 40 MW) of hybrid renewable power under the SPV model with agreements expected to be finalised in Q2 FY 2026-27, and has signed an MOU with GMDC to explore additional renewable assets in SPV mode.

- Throughout FY 2025-26 the prices of chlor-alkali products were under pressure due to various geographical issues as well as moderate demand from all the key segments, although the caustic soda segment recovered towards the year end.
- The Company availed External Commercial Borrowing of USD 68.70 Million to part finance expansion, and made a pre-payment of USD 34.35 Million along with a half yearly installment of USD 6.87 Million due to high currency fluctuations. It availed a term loan from HDFC Bank to repay the ECB, secured against the assets of the CLM plant at Dahej, repayable in five half yearly installments with the last repayment on 17th March 2028.
- A Competition Commission of India investigation into alleged contravention of Section 3(1) read with 3(3)(d) of the Competition Act, 2002 in respect of sales of chemical products to the Delhi Jal Board resulted in a penalty order which the Company has appealed before the NCLAT. The NCLAT granted a stay subject to a deposit of 10% of the penalty amount, and the matter is at the stage of final arguments.
- Several projects are under implementation at once, including the Chlorotoluene Downstream Plant, the Caustic Soda Flaking Plant, the HCl Synthesis Unit and the Cell Element Replacement Project, all targeted for commissioning during FY 2026-27, alongside multiple renewable SPVs. The Hydrazine Hydrate Plant remains under a stabilization phase with production levels still being improved gradually.
- A material part of the planned power-cost reduction depends on third-party SPVs with Aditya Birla Renewable Energy, Clean Max and GIPCL, plus short and medium-term solar purchase arrangements, so delayed commissioning of any of these projects would delay the cost benefit.

strategy.body:

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.

hero.oneLiner: Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Limited, promoted by the Government of Gujarat and established in 1973, is one of India's leading chlor-alkali producers, having grown from an initial 37,425 TPA of caustic soda in 1976 to an aggregate 8,73,750 MTPA (including GNAL).
